relationships.evidence_quote: Collectively, these results demonstrate that CGRP activation effectively curbs not only addictive-like behavior induced by optical stimulation of dopamine neurons but also behavior induced by cocaine administration.

relationships.subject: parabrachial CGRP neurons

relationships.subject: parabrachial CGRP neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Interestingly, with single stimulation, only the activation of CGRP terminals in the CeA significantly diminished lever-pressing behavior compared to the eYFP group (Fig. 4C).

key_findings: Optogenetic activation of parabrachial CGRP neurons suppresses dopamine self-stimulation and cocaine self-administration without nocifensive responses.
Silencing PBN CGRP neurons blocks footshock-induced suppression of addictive-like behavior; CeA terminals are the effective downstream target.
